newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat falls in active trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat falls in active trade.

text.p: Australian wheat futures traded actively in a falling market on Friday on fears that further significant price falls loomed.
A total of 71 lots changed hands, with the January, March, May and November 1997 contracts all falling by between A$5.00 and A$6.00 a tonne.
"Basically ... people are worried that it could go lower," said Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd.
This was despite one school of thought among merchants that the Australian Standard White price could not fall lower than its current level of around A$145.00, he said.

This was based on the belief that, after transport charges, it was hardly worthwhile growing wheat at A$100.00-A$110.00 a tonne. This would cause growers to stockpile or to sell only to the Australian Wheat Board pool, he said.

The other school of thought was that the huge amount of wheat Australia was producing this year would take well into 1998 to sell. As a result, all contract months would come under selling pressure as January and February approached, he said.
Ord Minnett chartists were looking for January futures to fall to A$130.00 a tonne now that A$150.00 had been broken.
